title: The towers defining integral pullback and completed tensor product are invariant under change of K-flat resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\geq1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_W$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with projections $\pi_n$, restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ along $\pi_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and derived category $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a tower $(C_n,t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n)_{n\geq1}$ of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$-modules write $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}(C_\bullet)$ for the complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, where $1-s:\prod_nC_n\to\prod_nC_n$, $(c_n)\mapsto(c_n-t_n(c_{n+1}))$, on the termwise products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. For a complex $P$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$-modules put $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}(A_{E,n})_W$ (termwise change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), with the maps $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ induced by $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $f^*=f^{-1}(-)\otimes_{f^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y}(A_{E,n})_X$ the module inverse image on sheaves of $(A_{E,n})_Y$-modules [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For complexes $P$ on $Y$ and $P,Q$ on $W$ define

$$
 T_f(P)=\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_n\operatorname{Res}_nf^*(P_n),\qquad
 T(P,Q)=\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_n\operatorname{Res}_n\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{(A_{E,n})_W}Q_n)\bigr),
$$

with direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and transition maps induced by those of $P_\bullet$, $Q_\bullet$. Then: (1) if $u:P\to P'$ and $v:Q\to Q'$ are quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,-}$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the induced maps $T_f(P)\to T_f(P')$ and $T(P,Q)\to T(P',Q')$ are quasi-isomorphisms; (2) consequently, choosing for every object a K-flat resolution with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $K\mapsto T_f(P_K)$ and $(M,N)\mapsto T(P_M,P_N)$ define functors $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)^2\to D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, independent of the resolutions up to a unique isomorphism of functors compatible with their natural comparison isomorphisms on K-flat representatives (these comparisons identify the descended functor with the displayed complex construction after localization), and each value is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of the corresponding tower in $D(-_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: The canonical finite reduction transition is semilinear for the finite quotient map, by unrestrictedIntegralTransition_smul. Retype it as an actual finite-module morphism. The constant coefficient direct-image maps commute with the quotient, by the constant sheafification adjunction unit. Take the adjunction mate of the finite reduction map to construct each finite pullback transition, and use its naturality to assemble a natural chain map. Restrict along the completed projections, whose compatibility is the inverse-limit cone equation.

The constant quotient map is locally surjective and factors through the completed projection, so that projection is locally surjective. Full faithfulness of restriction along a locally surjective ring map lets a completed-linear map lift to the finite coefficient ring. The pullback adjunction then shows that equality on the unit generators determines it. The mate unit formula supplies the required generator equation, proving the pullback transition existence and uniqueness without a choice of unconstrained data.

Transpose each finite semilinear chain map under the existing scalar-extension adjunction. Apply the normalized signed-total tensor comparison to the two transposes, then transpose back. The existing homogeneous-generator equations and adjunction unit equation give the required pure-tensor formula. Naturality follows by equality on homogeneous pure tensors: the formula for each composite reduces it to naturality of the two given finite reduction maps. Compare the module-unit generator with the original toSheafify generator for arbitrary commutative ring sheaves before specializing to integral coefficients. Restrict the chain map along the compatible completed projections. Local surjectivity of the upper projection lets a completed-linear map lift to the finite coefficient ring; sheafified pure-tensor extensionality and direct-sum extensionality prove uniqueness. Keep the original operation data and propositions definitionally equal. Factor repeated coefficient-forgetful functors, section evaluation, termwise scalar restriction and the original curried signed-total tensor composite through transparent item-local definitions. Record the scalar-extension chain adjunction once in a private definition. These share elaborated data without changing the functors or propositions. The naturality proof compares the curried total map with the simultaneous signed-total map, and then applies scalar-restriction naturality to the finite semilinear tensor square.

The specified ordinary reduction functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes by the existing independent-coefficient K-flat invariance theorem applied to its canonical object and map equations. Independent-universe tensor cancellation and change-of-rings K-flat preservation show that the reduced complexes are K-flat. Apply the already proved left and right tensor quasi-isomorphism helpers from the ringed-site derived tensor descent module, and compose the two induced maps. These helpers supply the mapping-cone and signed-flip comparisons without repeating their constructions.

For the exact specified constant-coefficient pro-etale pullback, transport the sites to coefficient-sized models, normalize the ring inverse-image comparison by the constant-section unit, and identify the underlying module pullback with exact inverse image of abelian sheaves. Restriction of scalars is exact because the underlying abelian sheaf is unchanged. Consequently the strict pullback and tensor tower maps are levelwise quasi-isomorphisms.

Prove strict Roos invariance first in an arbitrary abelian category with exact countable products. Exact products make the product map a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the existing mappingCone.quasiIso_map_of_quasiIso theorem to the square for 1-s. The recorded homotopyCofiber map agrees with mappingCone.map by its summand inclusions. Shift and reflection by Q give the generic result. Specialize it to the completed coefficient category using exact pro-etale countable products. Exactness of products in the completed coefficient category is supplied directly by Scheme.ProEt.products_exact, avoiding a duplicated epi-preservation proof.

Use the existing flat_representative_localization theorem to establish localization of the good complexes, identifying its object property by propositional extensionality. Retain goodComplexes_isLocalization with its original proposition (using transparent coefficient-forgetful aliases) as a wrapper for import-all consumers. A generic localization_factor_exists helper packages Localization.lift and Localization.fac before specializing to the strict pullback and tensor functors. Fully faithful precomposition, also for the product localization, gives the unique compatible comparison isomorphisms.

In an arbitrary abelian category with exact countable products, the proved countable-product comparison identifies Q of a termwise product with the derived-category product, preserving its projections. Projection extensionality identifies Q(1-s) with the derived transition endomorphism. Transport the distinguished mapping-cocone triangle along this isomorphism to prove the generic Roos derived-limit property. Specialize it to completed coefficient modules. For an arbitrary representative isomorphism, apply the descended functor to its inverse, compose with its representative comparison, and transport the triangle. Repeat for the product of representatives in the tensor case. Conjunction introduction combines the clauses.

proof_origin.note: The tensor transition is proved without new holes or arbitrary coefficient data. All returned edits to coefficient/reduction modules, explicit operation return types and the TensorLevel implicit_reducible attribute are dropped. Seven public item-local transparent definitions share repeated functor, evaluation, termwise scalar restriction and tensor-composite data. The change record lists all thirteen original declarations whose headers or non-theorem bodies change, with definitionally equal old/new expressions; the two public transition theorems and liftMap_apply keep their original statements verbatim (reviewer correction: the wrapped forms broke rw in unchanged consumers). Every original declaration remains. All existing non-theorem bodies except TensorLevel and the private coefficient projection remain verbatim; restrictComplexMap has a definitionally equal header. The original curried signed-total tensor functor data is retained. The private adjunction cache changes proof construction only. No extra public cochain-instance import is introduced, no consumer is adapted, and no module is withdrawn. The eight newly added private proof definitions use no_expose; no original declaration receives that attribute.
